commitments.claim: Restructuring plan announced May 13, 2026: pre-tax charges of up to $1 billion, of which Cisco expects to recognize approximately $450 million in Q4 FY26 with the remainder during fiscal 2027, to fund investment in silicon, optics, security and AI.

AI infrastructure from hyperscalers: $5.3 billion of orders taken year to date; expected FY26 orders raised to $9 billion (from $5 billion) and expected FY26 AI revenue raised to $4 billion (from $3 billion).
Major multi-year, multi-billion-dollar campus networking refresh cycle underway, with campus orders up >25% and data center switching orders up >40% year over year.
Quarterly dividend of $0.42 per share declared, paid July 22, 2026.
$9.6 billion remaining authorization under the stock repurchase program with no termination date.
Pursuit of strategic investments in innovation to capture AI-era infrastructure opportunities (CFO commentary alongside raised FY26 guidance).

thesis.what_must_be_true: Hyperscaler AI networking capex must remain intact through FY27 so the $9B FY26 order book converts to revenue at gross margins near 65%; the campus/branch refresh must stay a multi-year, broad-based cycle that absorbs the ~$1B restructuring reinvestment; tariff policy must not worsen beyond what is embedded in guidance; and inventory build (up $1.5B over nine months) must convert to shipments rather than write-downs. If AI orders decelerate while enterprise refresh demand proves pulled forward, the FY27 revenue bridge collapses and the multiple should de-rate.

validated.preview_note: Cisco closes fiscal 2026 on August 13 having beaten the high end of guidance in all three reported quarters, and the setup again favors a beat-and-raise. Guidance calls for Q4 revenue of $16.7-16.9B and non-GAAP EPS of $1.16-1.18, with FY26 at $62.8-63.0B and $4.27-4.29. We model Q4 revenue of $17.1B (+16% Y/Y) and non-GAAP EPS of $1.18, with FY26 landing at $63.2B and $4.28. Three factors matter most. First, AI conversion: with $5.3B of hyperscaler orders already booked against a raised $9B FY26 target and AI revenue raised to $4B, the question is whether Q4 shipments stretch ahead of our estimate. Second, the campus refresh: networking orders grew >50% in Q3; sustained double-digit campus and data-center switching momentum validates the multi-year cycle narrative. Third, the new restructuring: ~$450M of charges hit Q4, with the balance in FY27, so GAAP EPS prints at the top of the $0.80-0.85 guide only if underlying margins hold near 64% GAAP gross margin. The reaction hinges on the FY27 guide: we expect Q1 revenue of $16.2-16.4B and non-GAAP EPS of $1.09-1.11; anything implying FY27 below ~$66B will disappoint, while an AI orders outlook above $9B for FY27 extends the momentum trade.
validated.reasoning:
Anchors come entirely from the filed record: Q3 FY26 8-K (0000858877-26-000075) supplies the latest quarter actuals (revenue $15,841M, GAAP EPS $0.85, non-GAAP EPS $1.06, CFO $3,757M), current Q4/FY26 guidance, the $450M Q4 restructuring estimate, the raised $9B AI orders / $4B AI revenue expectations, and capital allocation facts ($0.42 dividend, $9.6B remaining buyback authorization). Prior quarters come from the Q1/Q2 FY26 and Q4 FY25 8-Ks.

Q4 FY26 revenue of $17.1B is $200M above the guidance high end, consistent with Cisco beating the high end by $33M/$149M/$241M in Q1-Q3 while orders accelerated (product orders +35%, networking orders >+50%). A ~$1.26B Q4 revenue step-up is supported by the back-half weighting of the $4B AI revenue target and Q4 seasonality (Q4 was +$524M vs Q3 in FY25). GAAP gross margin of 63.8% sits within the 63.5-64.5% guide; non-GAAP gross margin of ~65.9% and non-GAAP operating margin of ~34.8% sit inside the guided 65.5-66.5% and 34-35% bands. The full ~$450M restructuring charge is booked in Q4 per the May 13 disclosure, keeping GAAP EPS at $0.85 (top of guide) while non-GAAP EPS reaches $1.18. Interest expense rises modestly on the larger debt stack (Q3 issuances of $6.4B). GAAP tax at ~16% matches guidance.

Cash flow: Q4 is seasonally the strongest cash quarter (FY25 Q4 CFO was $4,234M); I model CFO of $4,477M tempered by continued inventory build for the refresh/AI ramp, capex of $400M (FY26 capex $1,420M vs $905M FY25 as Cisco invests in labs/silicon test capacity), buybacks of $1.4B and the $0.42 dividend ($1,660M, declared in May, paid July 22, 2026). The balance sheet rolls forward mechanically: cash falls to $6,140M with modest net debt repayment, and retained earnings roll to $1,036M.

FY26 totals: revenue $63,173M (above the $63.0B guide top), non-GAAP EPS $4.28 (top of $4.27-4.29), FCF ~$11.85B. FY27 builds on a normalizing but still strong cycle: Q1 guide of $16.2-16.4B (I expect a beat to $16.35B), FY27 revenue ~$68B (+7.6%), non-GAAP EPS ~$4.67, capex ~$1.6B and FCF ~$13.35B as working-capital intensity fades. FY28/FY29 assume growth decelerating toward 5-6% with EPS growing faster on buybacks and expanding software/services mix.
